sam_filters.question: Must be a degree-granting body with an innovation function
sam_filters.rule: universities + colleges; standalone diploma institutes excluded (no innovation mandate)
sam_filters.note: Stand-alone institutions (12,002) are polytechnics, teacher-training and nursing institutes at diploma level. They have no IIC and no NIRF Innovation obligation. Excluding them removes 20% of the registered base.

sam_filters.question: Must have institutional internet, not just computers in a room
sam_filters.rule: universities x NKN share + colleges x NKN share
sam_filters.note: THE FINDING. Colleges have a computer centre in 88% of cases but institutional backbone connectivity in only 24%. A cloud product needs the backbone; the upper bound assumes computer-centre presence suffices.

sam_filters.question: Must demonstrably file an innovation return
sam_filters.rule: count of institutions that filed the Innovation category in 2025
sam_filters.note: The only filter with a directly observed count. Everything upstream of this is a proxy; this is 777 institutions that demonstrably did the work.

sam_filters.question: Must be able to afford the contract
sam_filters.rule: Rs 1.2L is 0.0063% of a NIT budget and 0.3% of the LOW end of the bounded private college revenue band
sam_filters.note: PASSES 100%. This filter excludes nobody, at either price. That is the Phase 5 result restated: affordability has never been the obstacle.

som_capacity.method: Capacity-built. Derived from the seeded Monte Carlo, not from ambition.

rejected_plan.why: todo.md PHASE 7 proposed 5 / 15 / 40-50 institutions. The year-3 figure implies ~50 paying institutions, a sales team that does not exist, and a conversion rate nobody has measured. We reject it and model capacity instead.

som_capacity.note: Capacity is the binding constraint, and it binds HARD: the binding limit is conversion (r=0.65), which is precisely the quantity no interview has measured.

state_sotp.acv_basis: Analyst range. No state portal procurement value is published anywhere. Anchored on the observation that a state portal must serve a whole-state ecosystem and is a scored national deliverable - but this is PRIOR, not evidence.
state_sotp.attainable_basis: Zero to eight of 34 over three years. A state portal decision is a ministerial one; it is not a founder-led sales motion and it does not compound the way institutional licences do.
state_sotp.caveat: Sized separately and on the PRIOR tier. The whole point of segment G9 is that it is the only ACT NOW quadrant - but ACT NOW means the forcing event is strong, not that the sale is easy. Treat this as an option, not a plan.
state_sotp.forcing_event: SRF evaluation cycle; results published each January

penetration.interpretation: Only 1.32% of registered higher education institutions file a NIRF Innovation return, while 24-28% hold an IIC. The gap between those two numbers - roughly 13,000 institutions that are mandated to report and do not - is the structural headroom. It is also the population most likely to be unready, which is why digital readiness (filter 2) and innovation activity (filter 3) remove most of them.

triangulation_verdict.finding: The ceiling methods and the reachable method are NOT supposed to agree, and we refuse to average them. Their gap is the single most useful number here.
triangulation_verdict.rule: M1 and M2 are ceilings: they state what would exist if we won every eligible institution. The reachable method applies an explicit adoption-and-capture band. Report both. The ratio between them is the growth headroom an investor is buying.
triangulation_verdict.precedent: Phase 5 recorded conflict C-05: two research houses size the SAME market 625x apart (US$499M vs US$0.8M). Published sizing in this category is demonstrably unusable. That is why M1 is built bottom-up from institution counts and budget documents rather than from a report.
triangulation_verdict.investor_note: A TAM is a ceiling, not a forecast. The number to underwrite is SOM, which is capacity-built and roughly two orders of magnitude below TAM. Anyone showing one TAM number without its method is asking you to trust a method they have not shown you. Ours are all three, and one of them is the bad news.

falsifiers.what_would_break_it: NIRF Innovation filers turn out to file for a compliance minimum with no reporting burden worth paying to remove
falsifiers.threshold: If 3 of 6 interviewed filers describe the return as near-zero-effort, SAM collapses toward the IIC registration count rather than the filer count

falsifiers.what_would_break_it: Cloud delivery makes institutional backbone irrelevant
falsifiers.threshold: If on-premise demand falls below 20% (H-10 prior lower bound) then the 24% NKN figure stops being a constraint and SAM roughly doubles
falsifiers.observable: OQ-30 / H-10; currently 0% of institutions observed

falsifiers.what_would_break_it: Emerging-tier states turn out to be the best prospects (most to gain, least incumbent)
falsifiers.threshold: If Emerging-tier states are easier to convert than established ones, the haircut is removed and SAM rises to the full 777
falsifiers.observable: No Emerging-tier state report obtainable (Phase 6) - untestable today

falsifiers.what_would_break_it: Conversion turns out much higher than the 2-20% prior
falsifiers.threshold: Conversion above 30% would make capacity, not conversion, the binding constraint and would justify hiring ahead of revenue

falsifiers.claim: Scenario B is a real price
falsifiers.what_would_break_it: it is not - every rupee in Scenario B is aspirational
falsifiers.threshold: Any single signed contract at or above Rs 5 lakh per year

falsifiers.claim: The state layer is an option worth pursuing
falsifiers.what_would_break_it: State portals are politically untouchable or already outsourced to a consortium
falsifiers.threshold: One state nodal officer describing the portal as fixed or out of scope
falsifiers.observable: No Nodal Officer has been spoken to
